prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1248; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a low-speed collision in a parking lot involving the insured vehicle and a second vehicle. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the first notice of loss and the initial statements. The other driver confirms the accident happened as described, and the scene photos are consistent with that account.

Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant's attorney to confirm the injury claim is for a knee injury. The attorney has been asked to provide the medical records and any prior treatment history for that area.

Entry 4: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant inside the vehicle at the time of impact. Two witness statements also agree with the sequence of events as reported.

Entry 5: Inspected the vehicle. The damage pattern matches the impact described by all parties, and no earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior records or the body shop history.

Entry 6: Reviewed the claimant's statements from each contact so far. The account has stayed the same in every conversation, with no change in the sequence of events or the position of the vehicles.

Entry 7: Received the initial medical report. It is not yet clear whether the knee injury was caused by this crash, and the treating provider has not yet linked the condition to the collision.

Entry 8: Records from the claimant's prior care show a small strain in the same area several years ago. That strain healed fully, and the file notes it for comparison purposes only.

Entry 9: Treatment has followed a usual course, with visits tapering as the patient improved. The billing and treatment dates have been logged and are being reviewed against the recovery timeline.

Entry 10: Confirmed that nothing in the file suggests the vehicle damage occurred before the coverage start date. The driver is a household member of the policyholder and is covered as such under the policy.

Entry 11: Causation for the knee injury remains open pending the full medical review. Next steps are to request the complete treatment notes from the provider and to schedule a follow-up with the attorney's office.
